topics.topic: Deterministic ordering and failure precedence when multiple mapped lists are assembled or oversized
questions: When more than one delivered mapped output list exceeds the ceiling, which list is named in the result, or is the result intentionally not list-specific?
If two delivered value-list outputs exceed the ceiling, what does the operation return, and in what deterministic port order is the reported list selected?
In what order are delivered output lists built and measured, and does an oversized-list result stop further reads or lose to an `internal_error` encountered on another list?

quotes: assemble_mapped_lists: [BEHAVIOR] MUST build, for each MappedList in the order given, the list its elements' outputs make in element order, and write and publish nothing: a value list is one StoredValue whose bytes are canonical_bytes of the list of the elements' values — each read with read_value_bytes —, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) as items, of the class highest_disclosure_class gives for the elements' StoredValues — read through read_records with one RecordsById naming their value_ids —, its value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent; a file list is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements' SpooledFilesRefs.

assemble_mapped_lists: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST measure every value list against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant before it answers anything, and when the canonical bytes of any exceed it answer ListsOverCeiling naming the node and the first such port in the order given, with no list; it is given only the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output, so every delivered list of a node is measured before any of them is written or delivered.
judgement.why: The later notes require processing in the supplied order and select the first oversized port in that order after measuring all value lists.

quotes: deliver_input: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST take the value the source names and write it before anything reads or checks it: a RecordedSource names a written record; a ListElementSource first makes its list written as that list's own source says, then over a StoredValuesRef takes the element at map_index of the JSON array its StoredValue holds (read_value_bytes) as its own StoredValue of the receiving port's value_schema and the list's class — its bytes canonical_bytes of the element, value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding them and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent —, and over a SpooledFilesRef the file at that position, as a SpooledFilesRef of that one file with the list's disclosure_class; a MappedListSource names its AssembledList's value. A StoredValue that is not yet written — a list element, a mapped node's value list — MUST be published with put_value_bytes and written with record_change in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange under the given actor before fit_port_value checks it and before the reference is returned; an equal value already written is returned in its place.

plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] Each element's sources are one per input port in port name order: a RecordedSource for a flow input's StoredValuesRef, a constant's StoredValuesRef or the output ref of an unmapped succeeded node on the enabled edge — from its NodeExecution or its ElementSucceeded outputs —; a MappedListSource with the AssembledList of a mapped node's output; a ListElementSource with the list's own source and the element's map_index for a mapped element's map_over port. A guard's source node is never mapped (flows' proof), so a guard reads a written StoredValue. A flow output's source is formed the same way; an output reached by an edge straight from a flow input is that input's StoredValuesRef (A13 rule 3).
judgement.why: The later notes define the three source variants, the unpersisted AssembledList handoff and the source descriptor returned for flow outputs.

topics.topic: Whether new drafts must be persisted and replanned before executing ready work
questions: Are the returned next node, waits, outputs and status computed as if all returned drafts already existed, and must `runs` persist the drafts and call `plan_run` again before executing anything?
If one plan contains new skip or upstream-failure drafts and also a ready node, must `runs` first persist all drafts and call `plan_run` again, or may it execute the returned node from the same plan?

If a plan contains both newly determined drafts and a ready node, must `runs` persist all drafts and the derived run state before executing that node, or may it execute first and batch the drafts later?

quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity with when_missing unknown_reference, its pinned graph with read_flow_version and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, build its RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError, and then repeat, reading the trace again after every change: ask plan_run; when it derived drafts, write them in one RecordRunProgressChange; otherwise, when it names a next node, take that node's elements in the order given, as the next notes say; otherwise write the final change and stop. Every change goes through record_change with the given actor, and every time comes from kernel_now at the moment the field names.
judgement.why: The later orchestration gives drafts precedence, persists them, rereads the trace and replans before any returned ready node is executed.

topics.topic: Durable reference and disclosure class for an empty mapped file output
questions: How is the disclosure class of an empty mapped file-output list represented durably in the NodeExecution?
What exact reference does the empty-list NodeExecution store for an empty file output, and where is its disclosure class persisted so readers can compute the execution class after restart?

quotes:
`SpooledFilesRef`
    gains `disclosure_class`, the class of the file list it names, so an empty
    list keeps the class A13 rule 6 gives it and counts in an execution's
    class (A07 rule 5).

empty_list_outputs: [BEHAVIOR] MUST build, for each output port in port name order, an empty list of the class highest_disclosure_class gives for every input the node received — the mapped list and every other input, a StoredValuesRef counting with its StoredValue's class read through read_records with RecordsById (made only when there is a value_id to name), a SpooledFilesRef with its disclosure_class —: for a value port a StoredValue of the canonical bytes of [] with the canonical array schema with the port's stored schema as items, its bytes published with put_value_bytes, value_digest and value_id computed as for any StoredValue; for a file port an empty SpooledFilesRef. It writes no record: the StoredValue is written in the change of the node's one NodeExecution, which names these outputs.
judgement.why: The later contract adds disclosure_class to SpooledFilesRef, including empty lists, and makes that reference the file-port output named by the execution.

topics.topic: Element conclusion after not_applied resolution and before a fresh approval request
questions: What conclusion is returned during the committed gap after `resolve_attempt(not_applied)` but before `request_approval`, when the element needs owner approval but no requested approval exists?
What conclusion is returned for an element whose latest unknown attempt is resolved `not_applied` but which has no fresh requested approval yet?

quotes: operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly return ElementWaiting for owner approval with no approval_id during the post-resolution gap.

topics.topic: Idempotent reuse of already persisted or equal delivery StoredValues
questions: What happens when the same derived list element or mapped list is delivered again and its StoredValue already exists?
What must `record_delivery_values` do when an equal StoredValue already exists, including after a restart between the delivery-value write and the receiving NodeExecution write?

When the flow-output source is already a persisted StoredValue, must this operation make no store change, reuse it through an idempotent `record_delivery_values` call, or create another delivery record?

quotes: deliver_input: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST take the value the source names and write it before anything reads or checks it: a RecordedSource names a written record; a ListElementSource first makes its list written as that list's own source says, then over a StoredValuesRef takes the element at map_index of the JSON array its StoredValue holds (read_value_bytes) as its own StoredValue of the receiving port's value_schema and the list's class — its bytes canonical_bytes of the element, value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding them and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent —, and over a SpooledFilesRef the file at that position, as a SpooledFilesRef of that one file with the list's disclosure_class; a MappedListSource names its AssembledList's value. A StoredValue that is not yet written — a list element, a mapped node's value list — MUST be published with put_value_bytes and written with record_change in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange under the given actor before fit_port_value checks it and before the reference is returned; an equal value already written is returned in its place.

record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.

record_flow_output: [BEHAVIOR] A RecordedSource MUST answer its ref; a MappedListSource MUST publish its list's StoredValue with put_value_bytes and write it in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange through record_change under the given actor before answering its ref; it checks nothing, since a flow output holds the value its edge delivered and is of value carriage (A05 rule 7).
judgement.why: The later notes require reuse of an equal existing StoredValue and make already-recorded flow-output sources return their reference without another change.

topics.topic: Module responsible for persisting non-empty mapped value lists
questions: Which module calls the store change that creates a mapped node's value-list StoredValue: `runs` or `run_values`?
Which module owns writing the StoredValue record for a non-empty mapped node's delivered value list: `runs` or `run_values`?

quotes: | `record_delivery_values` | `run_values` | StoredValues M21 a run derives for delivery and no NodeExecution names: a list element a mapped element receives, a mapped node's value list (decision 32) |
judgement.divergence: One implementation has runs call the store change for the mapped value list, while another has run_values call record_delivery_values; the store boundary and module dependency checks observe which module performs the write.
judgement.why: State 2 assigns the first-delivery write to runs, while State 5 assigns the named change exclusively to run_values.

topics.topic: Permitted wall-clock use without making run planning nondeterministic
questions: May `plan_run` read the current wall clock, and if so which output fields use it without making the plan differ across reads or restarts?
For what operation may `run_graph` read `kernel_now`, and may the clock reading affect `plan_run`'s returned drafts or other output?

quotes: plan_run: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST trust the run, context, flow version and trace it is given and write nothing; it reads value bytes with read_value_bytes and every time a draft names from kernel_now.
judgement.why: The later notes permit wall-clock reads only to populate timestamps of newly derived drafts, while the structural planning decision remains trace-derived.

topics.topic: Plan representation of a recordless oversized mapped-list failure
questions: How does the plan represent a mapped node failed by an oversized derived list so that `runs`, dependants, run status and missing flow outputs all interpret it identically?
How is this recordless mapped-node failure represented in the plan so that `runs` can derive the run as failed, create dependent `upstream_failed` drafts, and report the same result after restart?

quotes: plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] A mapped node's elements are the positions of the list delivered to its map_over port, counted from the JSON array its StoredValue holds — read with read_value_bytes, or the canonical_json of an AssembledList not yet written — or the files of its SpooledFilesRef; a mapped node over an empty list is ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index whose sources are the node's inputs; a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded, succeeded only when all succeeded. For a succeeded mapped node with elements, the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output are asked of assemble_mapped_lists, an output no edge takes being asked nothing: ListsOverCeiling makes the node failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, with no record of its own and every element record staying as it is.

plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] When nothing is derived and no node is ready, the status is: when any element waits, awaiting_approval if one waits with reason owner_approval and otherwise pending, with one WaitingPoint per waiting element — a mapped operation node's elements being the positions of its delivered list; when nothing waits, succeeded when every node concluded succeeded or skipped_by_guard and failed otherwise, a mapped node whose delivered list is over the ceiling counting as failed. While a draft is derived or a node is ready the status is running. The outputs are those produced so far, whatever the status (A13 rule 7), each named by its flow output port; once the status has ended (= models.RunStatus: succeeded, failed or refused here) every other flow output is a MissingOutput with reason skipped_by_guard when every edge into it was disabled or comes from a node concluded skipped_by_guard and not_produced otherwise (= models.OutputReason).
judgement.why: The later notes represent the condition as ListsOverCeiling, treat the mapped node as failed without a record and derive dependant failures, final status and missing outputs from that condition.

topics.topic: Required NodeExecution draft fields and ownership of draft timestamps
questions: Which M23 fields must each draft contain, particularly `executed`, inputs, outputs, failure detail, `started_at` and `ended_at`, and which module supplies the timestamps before `record_run_progress`?

Does `run_graph` stamp the drafted skip and upstream-failure NodeExecutions, or does `runs` stamp them when `record_run_progress` is written; if `run_graph` calls the clock, what specified timestamp is it producing?

quotes: The conclusion of every element; each edge enabled, disabled or undecided; the `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` records that became determined, as drafts in (`node_id`, `map_index`) order; the next ready node with its elements and the source of each input; the waiting points; the produced outputs and, once ended, the reason per missing output; the status the run stops in.

Every timestamp an operation records comes from
  `clock.kernel_now`, taken at the moment the field names: a `started_at` when
  the execution or send begins — for an operation's NodeExecution, the
  `recorded_at` of its EffectAttempt when it has one (A11 rule 4) — every other
  time when its store change is made.
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns complete drafts already stamped by run_graph, while another returns only derived status and identity facts and lets runs fill empty inputs, outputs and details and stamp both times at persistence; trace readers observe different NodeExecution fields and timestamps.
judgement.why: State 5 requires NodeExecution drafts but does not fix their complete M23 projection or reconcile draft construction with the convention that non-start timestamps are taken when the store change is made.

topics.topic: State impact and failure behavior of publishing empty-list bytes
questions: Does `empty_list_outputs` call `store.put_value_bytes`, and if so what state impact and failure can that publication produce?
Is publishing `[]` part of this operation's state impact, and what result is returned if that publication fails?

quotes:
### Observable effect

The bytes of `[]` are published; no record is written.

### State impact

None; the caller writes `record_run_progress`.
judgement.divergence: One implementation calls store.put_value_bytes and can leave published content-addressed bytes, while another treats the operation as having no state impact and defers all mutation to the caller; the store and recovery cleanup observe the difference.
judgement.why: Publishing bytes changes the content-addressed store, directly contradicting the operation's stated absence of state impact.

topics.topic: Validation schema and stored schema for delivery-derived values
questions: Which schema is assigned to the StoredValue created for a mapped element before the receiving-port fit is checked?

Against which schema is a list element or mapped value list validated before `record_delivery_values` creates its StoredValue, and what schema does that StoredValue carry when the later receiving-port fit fails?

quotes: deliver_input: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST take the value the source names and write it before anything reads or checks it: a RecordedSource names a written record; a ListElementSource first makes its list written as that list's own source says, then over a StoredValuesRef takes the element at map_index of the JSON array its StoredValue holds (read_value_bytes) as its own StoredValue of the receiving port's value_schema and the list's class — its bytes canonical_bytes of the element, value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding them and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent —, and over a SpooledFilesRef the file at that position, as a SpooledFilesRef of that one file with the list's disclosure_class; a MappedListSource names its AssembledList's value. A StoredValue that is not yet written — a list element, a mapped node's value list — MUST be published with put_value_bytes and written with record_change in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange under the given actor before fit_port_value checks it and before the reference is returned; an equal value already written is returned in its place.

deliver_input: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST then check the written value with fit_port_value against port, with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for a value and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant for a file, the candidate a JsonCandidate of the value's canonical bytes, or a FileCandidate or FileListCandidate of the files' FileFacts read through read_records with SpooledFilesByKey, a read made only when there is a file to name, an empty list's candidate having no files; a misfit is answered, never raised, and the value stays written.
judgement.why: The later notes assign a sliced list element the receiving port's value_schema before persistence and then validate the written value against that same receiving port, leaving it stored on misfit.

topics.topic: deliver_input mapping of source-read, byte-publication, and persistence failures
questions: How are a missing source record, missing or corrupt source bytes, `put_value_bytes` failure, and refusal from `record_delivery_values` mapped by `deliver_input`?
What does `deliver_input` return when publishing the derived value's bytes fails before `record_delivery_values`, including an I/O failure or digest/size mismatch?

quotes:
### Errors

None of its own: a misfit is an answer; a failed store change is `internal_error`.

### Errors

`refused` when digest or size do not match; `internal_error` on a link or I/O
failure, nothing published.

A StoredValue that is not yet written — a list element, a mapped node's value list — MUST be published with put_value_bytes and written with record_change in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange under the given actor before fit_port_value checks it and before the reference is returned; an equal value already written is returned in its place.
judgement.divergence: One implementation propagates put_value_bytes RefusedError or a source UnknownReferenceError, while another converts every publication or source-integrity failure to internal_error; runs and the MCP caller observe different error codes and retry behavior.
judgement.why: Neither State 5 nor the later notes specify how deliver_input maps failures that occur before record_change, especially put_value_bytes refusal and missing or corrupt source data.
